evidence: Address/Run.hs:93-96 generateAndWriteKeyFiles generates one (vk, sk) pair and writes both; key-hash (:170-178) and build (:193-203) then independently parse the written vkey file, and operator.py:717-720 ties the built address's trailing 28 bytes to the CLI key hash. So the exported address is credential-matched to the same CLI-generated pair within the single key-gen operation. The operator deliberately never reads the skey and performs no signature test (:772 ownershipSignatureTestPerformed false); for an unfunded dedicated test wallet this source-grounded correspondence is adequate, and live ownership/spendability remains an open later question, as README.md:43 states. No new signature test needs to be imposed to call the resulting address a key-controlled test wallet.
summary: Keypair-to-address credential correspondence is established without opening the signing key; signature proof is correctly deferred, not required.

evidence: operator.py:457-549 performs each call via subprocess with PIPE and communicate(timeout). RLIMIT_FSIZE (:424, 32 MiB) does not bound pipe output, and RLIMIT_AS (:426) limits the child, not Python's buffering. Materiality is low for this fixed official code: with --out-file given, Address/Run.hs:181-182,221-223 and Info/Run.hs:73 write results to files, key-gen writes only files, so expected stdout/stderr is empty-to-small error text; the staged binary is hash-pinned to the official member, so a flooding binary would have to deviate from the mirrored source paths. Residual: a pathological binary could grow operator memory until the 30 s timeout/CPU limits fire; the attempt then fails spent with no address published. Not blocking for this fixed-code scope.
summary: Pipe output is technically unbounded in the parent, but materially bounded by the fixed official out-file code paths.

evidence: operator.py:422-426 sets RLIMIT_CPU (15,16), FSIZE 32 MiB, NOFILE 128, AS 4 GiB per CLI process (preexec_fn :514). No RLIMIT_CORE is set in set_limits, so core-dump behaviour is inherited from however the operator process itself is launched; a crashed key-gen child holds signing-key material in memory. AUTH (AUTH_KEYS :54-83) has no field to pin an inherited core limit. GHC runtime compatibility with a 4 GiB address-space cap and bwrap user-namespace availability on the host are runtime unknowns that cannot be settled by source reading and must not be probed under this review.

summary: Per-call limits are set as claimed except core dumps, which depend on unpinned caller inheritance.
